scope: does the game ever call the receive helper 0x674EB0?

experiment.handshake: full ring bridge, phase 8, ring B consumed at ~280 packets/s
experiment.result: milestone histogram contains CRT entry / WinMain / Com Init / Initial fastfiles / Engine init / Menu command queue / Switch to main menu / Frontend tick / UI views -- and NO recv_helper entry. Total 16 milestone events, zero receive-helper hits.

meaning: the client's game-side receive helper 0x674EB0 is never invoked while it consumes ring B. The consumer of ring B is therefore not the game network path (at least not through 0x674EB0). Since CL_ParseServerMessage fired once earlier, the gamestate path must have reached the parser through a different call (or the one call happened before this breakpoint category was active).
implications: ring B is drained by something else (a bridge/side consumer), so the injected packets never enter the game's netchan receive path after the gamestate
this explains 'consumed but not parsed' and why the two receive checks were healthy when forced: there really is no game-side packet
next: identify who advances 0x7872C00: breakpoint the pop routine or scan for code that reads the ring constants
if the bridge itself drains ring B for its own forwarding, stop that consumer from eating the game's packets
otherwise make the game's receive path the consumer (call 0x674EB0 from the bridge's injection loop is not enough; the game must invoke it)
